actions.justification: Patient has worsening neurological status after tPA with signs of hemorrhagic transformation — immediate stroke team activation is the first mandatory step to coordinate urgent care.

Urgent non-contrast CT head is mandatory to evaluate for hemorrhagic transformation given neurological deterioration after tPA. BP 195/108 and SpO2 92% with Cushing-like HR of 55 raise concern for raised ICP from hemorrhage.
Mandatory neurological assessment to quantify deficit severity and establish a baseline for comparison, guiding urgency and treatment decisions.

Mandatory action - IV access is essential for medication administration, especially given this patient may need urgent reversal agents for post-tPA hemorrhage and BP management. BP is critically elevated at 195/108.
Mandatory action - hypoglycemia/hyperglycemia can mimic or worsen neurological symptoms and must be rapidly excluded and corrected. Critical in any stroke/neurological deterioration workup.

Mandatory action - CBC, BMP, and coagulation studies are essential to assess for coagulopathy post-tPA (especially fibrinogen, PT/INR), platelet count, and electrolyte abnormalities contributing to neurological deterioration.

MANDATORY action - required to evaluate cardiac rhythm, identify atrial fibrillation or other arrhythmias contributing to stroke etiology, and assess for cardiac complications in this neurologically deteriorating post-tPA patient.

MANDATORY action - critical to establish the timeline for tPA administration and assess whether the patient is within any additional intervention windows. Essential for guiding further treatment decisions including possible mechanical thrombectomy.

Optional but clinically relevant - establishing baseline functional status (pre-stroke mRS) is important for guiding treatment intensity decisions, ICU admission planning, and prognostication in this patient with post-tPA hemorrhagic transformation.

Per AHA stroke guidelines, CT head findings must be systematically evaluated using ASPECTS scoring to assess extent of hemorrhagic transformation and ischemic changes following tPA administration. Patient has worsening neuro status consistent with hemorrhagic transformation.

With suspected post-tPA hemorrhagic transformation and severely elevated BP (195/108), surgical risk assessment is needed to evaluate candidacy for potential neurosurgical intervention if hemorrhage is confirmed on CT.

Worsening neurological status post-tPA with hemodynamic instability (Cushing response pattern: hypertension + bradycardia, SpO2 92%) warrants immediate neurointerventional team activation for emergent evaluation and potential intervention.
